- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts show gradual upward drift, correct for overconfidence by reducing slope slightly and adding early volatility buffer.
- If recent sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and forecast is flat or rising, adjust downward by 3–5% to account for suppressed momentum.
- After sharp spikes in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast slope at 0.5–1.0% per day after peak.
- When official supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model often underestimates upside — add 2–4% upward bias to mean forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean — apply mean reversion with 1–2% decay per day.
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to account for event-driven volatility.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is linear, introduce 1–2% random walk noise to reflect uncertainty.
- When recent auction events are CAP3 EU or DE, model often overreacts — apply 5–10% downward correction to forecast peak if preceded by bullish sentiment.
